checks.reasoning: An orbit associated with nZ has n elements for n>0; the subgroup 0 gives an infinite orbit. Hence finiteness requires n_0=0, finite multiplicities n_i, and finitely many nonzero multiplicities; conversely these conditions give a finite sum of finite orbit sizes.
checks.outcome: Criterion checks under the stated orbit-count interpretation. The preceding family is nevertheless written a_i, not n_i.

checks.reasoning: On {1,2,3,4}, let u=(12)(34). There are two orbits of size 2, so n_2=2 and all other n_i vanish. Thus all n_i except at most one are zero, while u is not transitive.
checks.outcome: Sweep confirmed: the manuscript has the equivalence arrow, and the right-hand condition is insufficient. A single orbit would require sum n_i=1 for a nonempty transitive set.

checks.reasoning: The partitions of 2,3,4 number 2,3,5 and are represented by the displayed cycle types. A2 is trivial; A3 is cyclic of order 3 and therefore has three conjugacy classes. A 4-cycle has sign (-1)^3=-1.
checks.outcome: The live counts through S4 and A3 agree. The canceled A4 entry contains an odd 4-cycle, but it is left canceled and unrepaired. The written S5 question is not completed.

checks.reasoning: With p:G to Gamma and q:Gamma to G, qp is a map G to G, whereas id_Gamma is a map Gamma to Gamma. The expected section condition would instead compose pq.
checks.outcome: The legible central qp cannot literally have the written target identity under these arrows. Flanking overwritten marks may be correction material; their purpose is unresolved and no correction is imposed.
